The Second Temple period lasted from roughly 516 B.C. to 70 A.D., when Roman forces destroyed the temple during the First Jewish-Roman War.

Pictures released by Israeli police show the dark interior of the rock-cut burial cave, with debris scattered across the floor.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Israel Police and the Israel Antiquities Authority for additional comment.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Jerusalem has been inhabited for thousands of years, and remnants of its ancient past are still emerging today.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The cave is one of several archaeological finds recently uncovered in the Holy City.

Earlier this summer, officials announced the discovery of charred wooden beams in Jerusalem dating back roughly 2,600 years — likely remnants of the destruction of Solomon's Temple.

Another major find came last year, when archaeologists uncovered the longest and best-preserved section of Jerusalem's Hasmonean-era wall found to date.

item.title: Internet goes wild for Little League World Series player's extremely relatable dream job
item.description: The Little League World Series player questionnaire went viral after Daniel Huang from Vancouver's team revealed his hilariously relatable dream job.
item.content:encoded:
It has been around for as long as I can remember, but I think the Little League World Series player questionnaire really hit its stride when Big Al filled us all in on his habit of hitting dingers.

Well, it looks like we may have found a new LLWS player questionnaire all-star, and his name is Daniel Huang.

The center fielder for Canada's Little Mountain Little League out of Vancouver asked what his dream job is, and his answer was used during a recent game against South Korea. Man, oh man, did the internet ever get hit in the proverbial feels by this one.

LITTLE LEAGUE TEAM GETS ABSOLUTELY SCREWED ON FINAL PITCH OF NO-HITTER, FANS STUNNED BY CALL

I understand this. We all understand this.

Although I would suggest young Daniel here not have his eyes so fixed on his AARP that he forgets to enjoy his college years.

The beauty of the player questionnaire is you get a bunch of kids, many of whom are away from their parents for the first time in their lives, just lettin' it rip on these questions.

It's like "Kids Say The Darndest Things" without a certain former Jell-O spokesman MCing it all.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Of course, on social media, people were eating up Huang's answer that is so relatable to anyone who has ever worked a day in their life.

I mean, being retired does seem awesome. I can't even comprehend just going out and doing things on weekdays.

It must be like when you were a kid in the summer, and you'd lose track of what day of the week it was because it simply doesn't matter.

So retirement is basically one big fixed-income summer until you take a dirt nap.

What a way to go.

Unfortunately for the team from Canada, while they beat the youngsters from Seoul, South Korea, in the game with Huang's viral answer, they dropped their next game against the team from Tokyo, Japan.

item.title: Matthew Berry has had talks with ESPN about a return, following Pat McAfee model
item.description: Matthew Berry confirms he has talked to ESPN about a potential return, citing Pat McAfee's model, but says no deal is imminent with the network.
item.content:encoded:
Matthew Berry left ESPN in 2022, in part, because the company was not open to employees operating their own media companies. Berry then joined NBC, where he appeared on "Football Night in America" while building his own fantasy football company on the outside.

Berry has since departed NBC to focus on Fantasy Life, his independently owned media company on pace to generate eight figures in revenue this year.

ESPN has since changed its philosophy. Management is now open to partnering with talent who retain ownership of their content.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Berry spoke to OutKick this week on video about his career, business, and future. During the discussion, we asked whether he had talked to ESPN about a potential return in recent months.

"Yes," Berry responded without hesitation.

"I have [talked to ESPN]," he continued. "When you leave and go out on your own, you look at [Pat McAfee] as the great model. ESPN specifically has done it with some people [in that the talent either license their show to ESPN or can retain ownership of a media brand outside of the network]."

In addition to McAfee, Berry cited other unique agreements ESPN has made recently.

MATTHEW BERRY DISCUSSES WITH OUTKICK WHETHER HE'D HIRE DIANNA RUSSINI FOR HIS BUDDING FANTASY FOOTBALL EMPIRE

"Rich Eisen brought his show over [to ESPN] on a licensing agreement. They have other talent where they do not necessarily license the show, but they allow them to have outside businesses. You think about Bussin’ With The Boys or Josh Pate."

As Pate exclusively told OutKick, he and Bussin’ With The Boys co-hosts Will Compton and Taylor Lewan will host a new college football show on ESPN each Friday this season. Their podcast will remain separate.

"I’ll be honest," Berry added. "I have a very good relationship with Jimmy Pitaro and Burke Magnus. I have remained friendly with them over the years since I left."

Berry cautioned that, while the talks have been positive, "no deal is imminent" with ESPN.

Frankly, it would have been surprising if Berry and ESPN had not discussed a partnership. Berry’s digital content ranks among the most popular in sports media. During football season, his podcast downloads are on par with Barstool’s "Pardon My Take" and "The Bill Simmons Podcast."

He is an ideal fit for ESPN’s current strategy of teaming with the top digital creators in sports, with McAfee as the most notable example.

For the same reasons, we suspect Berry is also having conversations with Amazon, Netflix, Paramount, and various gambling providers about amplifying Fantasy Life.

Later in the interview, Berry said he will not take home as much money this year as he did in salary at ESPN. However, he expects to exceed his television salary by the third year.

item.title: NASCAR WAG holds on for dear life with her watermelon farmer boyfriend, Kirk's dog is back & Al vs Trump!
item.description: Ross Chastain's girlfriend Jordyn Mallory holds on for dear life during a Daytona ride-along as NASCAR gears up for a big weekend at the speedway.
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday–Friday on OutKick.com.

Final Friday of August. Can you believe it? We had 22 FCS games last night, and a couple were wild. What a return for football!

We have Bill Belichick in Dublin tomorrow. We have NASCAR in Daytona tomorrow. We have a full weekend of Sox-Yanks in the Bronx.

And yes, the Fever play tonight, which means we are obligated to cover it. But after tonight? We officially start spending our weekends watching football.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Live it up, WNBA! Your time is short. Let's roll.

Welcome to a Friday Nightcaps — the one where NASCAR WAG Jordyn Mallory goes for a test ride and holds on for dear life in a Daytona tuneup.

What else? I've got a couple insane moments from the world of FCS last night, Al Michaels still pumping his fastball and Kirk's dog, once again, being shoved down our throats.

Did y'all miss Kirk's dog?! Well, he's back! This guy is amazing. It HAS to be a bit at this point, right?

OK, let's get this show on the road. I've gotta head on up to Daytona for a big weekend of automobile racing, and I'd prefer to not hit the terrible stretch of traffic in Melbourne and Cocoa Beach.

Grab you a $11 Busch Light from the Daytona International Speedway infield — Lord knows I will — and settle in for a Friday 'Cap!

I took that picture a few years ago — the first Daytona 500 after Trump got re-elected — and all folks could talk about was Anheuser-Busch changing it from "Domestic" to "American" beer. That was a big story that week in the infield.

They never came out and admitted it, but it was very clearly because Trump was back in office and everyone was trying to cover their tails from the wokeness of the last four years. Hilarious.

Anyway, this will be my 11th summer race at Daytona, dating back to my years at the Daytona Beach News-Journal. Eleven! Time flies. My first ever race I covered was way back in 2016 — a month after I got married.

Fun fact from that race: I didn't know what to do or where to go. Had no idea. More importantly, I had no idea where I was ALLOWED to go.

So, naturally, I walked straight into a TV interview after a big wreck in an area that was very clearly restricted to just drivers.

If you scroll to the 2:00:25 mark, you'll see young, dumb, ignorant Zach on his phone as Jimmie and Jamie argue about the wreck:

I nearly got kicked out of the track once the PR folks figured it out. What a rush! And now, here we are, 11 years later and ready for another race weekend.

Can't wait.

On that note, here's Ross Chastain's girlfriend, Jordyn Mallory, going for a ride to help get us ready for the green flag:

Chastain, for those who don't know, is a seventh-generation watermelon farmer from down here in Alva, Florida. His family owns Chastain Farms.

True story.

He's also a good little driver, and probably ain't the worst bet at +3500. You never know with Daytona. This place is quite literally the Wild Wild West.

Carson Hocevar at +1600, Denny Hamlin at +2000 and Austin Dillon at +2800 probably aren't bad sprinkles, either.

You're welcome! (Or not)

OK, let's keep this class moving and head on up to Cleveland, where Al Michaels and Kirk Herbstreit got in a little preseason work last night and managed to take a dig at Donald J. Trump in the process:

"That is Lake Erie. We think it is still called Lake Erie... We're not quite sure at this point. But we'll be by Lake something like Ontario or whatever it's going to be called by the time we get to Buffalo. Anyway, you know what I'm talking about... Read the news."

Al! Some folks are pissed at Michaels today for mocking Trump's shiny new acquisition (Lake America!), while others loved it.

LONGTIME REPUBLICAN AL MICHAELS TOOK A JAB AT TRUMP AND NFL FANS WENT SPIRALING OUT OF CONTROL

Shockingly, the internet was divided on this one. That almost never happens! Al, by the way, has a long history of donating to the GOP. Not saying he's a Trump guy, but I'm certain he's not a Kamala guy.

OK, let's rapid-fire this Friday class into a big weekend. First up? You know what the internet is NOT divided over today?

Herbstreit's dog:

ENOUGH! I love Kirk Herbstreit. He's the best analyst in the game right now, in my opinion. Love him on GameDay. Love him on Thursday nights. Love him on Saturday nights.

But I'm so out on the dog shtick. I've been quietly out on it for years now, but, clearly, I don't need to be quiet anymore. Everyone is sick and tired of the dog. Peter is EVERYWHERE.

He's on the plane. On the field. In the booth. He's on the GameDay set every Saturday. It's too much.

Please, for the love of God, give Peter a rest this year. We're begging you.

Next? For those who didn't feel like subscribing to ESPN+ last night (all of you), we had an incredible first night of FCS football:

Amazing. What a start to the season! The best.

My question? What in the world is the point of ESPNU? There were 22 (!!!) FCS games last night, and the big-wigs in Bristol couldn't put one on ESPNU? What the heck is the point of that channel?! I was stunned.

Anyone else think it was odd?

OK, that's it for today — and this week. We haven't done enough baseball today, so here's umpire Laz Diaz accidentally trolling 70,000 fans in Atlanta last night.

See you Monday.

Was Al out of line? Email me at Zach.Dean@OutKick.com.
